title: Agent Skill Framework: Perspectives on the Potential of Small to Medium Language Models in Industrial Environments
abstract: arXiv:2602.16653v4 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Skills are getting increasingly used in recent agentic frameworks, performing robustly with proprietary LLMs. Yet, their effectiveness for small and medium-sized open-source models (270M--80B) remains underexplored, especially under industrial, resource-constrained conditions. As such, we present a large-scale empirical study evaluating the skill paradigm's feasibility across two open-source classification tasks: one insurance-claim task based on proprietary data, and a set of Python programming problems. We find that very small models frequently fail to retrieve or select correct skills, substantially limiting their usefulness in the evaluated skill-augmented settings, while larger 30B--80B models gain substantial benefits from skill augmentation. translated_title: 智能体技能框架：中小型语言模型在工业环境中的潜力展望
translated_abstract: 技能在近期的智能体（agentic）框架中得到越来越广泛的应用，其与专有大语言模型配合时表现稳健。然而，技能对中小型开源模型（270M–80B）的有效性仍未得到充分探索，尤其是在工业界资源受限的条件下。为此，我们开展了一项大规模实证研究，评估技能范式在两个开源分类任务上的可行性：一个是基于专有数据的保险理赔任务，另一个是一组Python编程问题。我们发现，极小型模型经常无法检索或选择正确的技能，这大大限制了它们在所评估的技能增强场景中的实用性；而较大的30B–80B模型则从技能增强中获得了显著收益。此外，我们还提供了面向部署的GPU性能画像，报告了在评估设置下各模型的显存-时间占用（GB·min）——这是一种面向部署场景的衡量指标。
tldr: 本研究通过大规模实证研究发现，技能增强范式能为30B–80B的中型开源模型带来显著收益，但极小型模型常常无法正确检索或选择技能，在工业资源受限场景下实用性有限。
en_tdlr: This large-scale empirical study finds that skill augmentation substantially benefits 30B–80B open-source models, while very small models frequently fail to retrieve or select correct skills, limiting their usefulness in resource-constrained industrial settings.
